transaction_summary.headline: GBP 657m equivalent new senior secured term loan, split into a $396m tranche and a EUR 418m tranche, to refinance Merlin's GBP 630m (equivalent) senior unsecured notes (SUNs) due November 2027
transaction_summary.borrower_entity: Announced by Merlin Entertainments Limited; borrower entity not disclosed - further diligence required (facility agreement). The RNS states that Merlin Entertainments Limited ('Merlin', together with its subsidiaries and affiliates, 'the Group') 'is pleased to announce that it has entered into commitment documentation' for the New Term Facility, but this identifies the announcing/group entity, not an explicit borrower or obligor designation for the facility itself. The SUNs being refinanced sit at Motion Bondco DAC. Source: Merlin RNS 'Merlin announces a new secured term loan financing to refinance its Senior Notes due 2027', 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/documents/ae93bb0a-d42e-4872-a856-3aefdaf949a1
transaction_summary.tranches_and_currencies: New Term Facility comprising a $396m tranche and a EUR 418m tranche, combined equivalent to approximately GBP 657m. Source: Merlin RNS, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/documents/ae93bb0a-d42e-4872-a856-3aefdaf949a1

pricing.margin: 650bps over the relevant benchmark (SOFR/EURIBOR), per 9fin sources. Source: 'Goldentree and Monarch lead Merlin refi as bonds and CDS take different rides', 9fin, 17-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/d2468584-df61-4bbb-99c2-19d9a2fc68de
pricing.cash_vs_pik: not available - further diligence required. 9fin's own analysis notes the coupon is 'not disclosed' by the company; likely source would be the facility agreement or a lender presentation once syndicated
pricing.oid_and_fees: not available - further diligence required. Likely source: facility agreement / syndication term sheet
pricing.estimated_all_in_cost: 9fin analysis assumes an all-in rate of at least 10%, consistent with other CCC+/Caa1-rated European senior secured paper, implying roughly GBP 65m of annual interest on GBP 657m of new debt versus roughly GBP 35m of coupon on the 4.5% EUR / 6.625% USD notes being refinanced - an estimated ~GBP 30m increase in annual interest expense. This is a 9fin estimate, not a disclosed figure. Source: 'Merlin refis SUNs as temporary fix - Mid-term cap stack risk remains', 9fin, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/7bbf2ed4-3a88-48dd-aaf8-3752b643a9d3

transaction_summary.maturity: Six years from closing, with a springing maturity that brings the due date forward to before 2030 if the company has not refinanced its other debt by then. Source: 'Goldentree and Monarch lead Merlin refi...', 9fin, 17-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/d2468584-df61-4bbb-99c2-19d9a2fc68de
transaction_summary.amortisation: not available - further diligence required. Likely source: facility agreement
transaction_summary.call_protection: not available - further diligence required. Likely source: facility agreement / syndication term sheet
transaction_summary.security_and_collateral: Secured alongside Merlin's existing senior secured debt, plus additional credit support from a portfolio of previously unencumbered UK assets: the London Eye, SEA LIFE London, Shrek's Adventure! London, and the UK Dungeons (London, York and Edinburgh) (together, 'the Portfolio'). Merlin retains full ownership and management of the Portfolio; no change for employees, visitors, ticket holders or memberships. Market feedback described the collateral pool as narrower than some investors had feared. Source: Merlin RNS, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/documents/ae93bb0a-d42e-4872-a856-3aefdaf949a1; 'Merlin confirms GBP 657m secured refi of 2027 SUNs', 9fin, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/b9ef800a-31a3-4e7d-9597-8492eac34786
transaction_summary.guarantees: not available - further diligence required (specific guarantor list for the New Term Facility not disclosed in public materials reviewed). Likely source: facility agreement. Note: the guarantor group for the existing 2032 SSNs, disclosed in the January 2025 Preliminary OM, included Motion Midco and a list of operating subsidiaries (e.g. Merlin Entertainments (Dungeons) Limited, Merlin Entertainments (SEA LIFE) Limited, Merlin Attractions Operations Limited, Motion Acquisition Limited, Motion Finco LLC, Motion Finco 2 S.a.r.l., among others) - the New Term Facility's guarantor package is not confirmed to match this list.
transaction_summary.ranking_vs_existing_debt: Ranks alongside (pari passu with) Merlin's existing senior secured debt (RCF, TLBs due 2029, SSNs due 2030/2031/2032), but benefits from additional collateral (the Portfolio) that the existing secured debt does not have. 9fin analysis flags this as a source of relative recovery dilution for existing secured holders, which it believes explains the divergent price action between the SUNs (rallied) and the 2030/2031/2032 SSNs (sold off) after the announcement. Source: 'Goldentree and Monarch lead Merlin refi...', 9fin, 17-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/d2468584-df61-4bbb-99c2-19d9a2fc68de; 'Merlin refis SUNs as temporary fix...', 9fin, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/7bbf2ed4-3a88-48dd-aaf8-3752b643a9d3
transaction_summary.covenants: Maintenance covenant package not disclosed for the New Term Facility - not available - further diligence required, likely source: facility agreement. Context on the existing secured stack: the RCF (GBP 428m facility) carries a springing net leverage covenant tested only when the facility is more than 40% drawn; Moody's expects compliance. Separately, a springing maturity covenant on the existing senior debt brings the RCF current if the SUNs are not refinanced/repaid before 15-Jul-2027, and brings the TLBs/SSNs current before 15-Aug-2027 - this is the mechanism the new facility is designed to defuse. Source: 'Merlin hires Kirkland amid 2027 refi pressure', 9fin, 09-Jun-2026, https://9fin.com/news/3311c31f-0997-468f-9aee-2f570c8ddb71; 'Arini trades Merlin Entertainment SUNs CDS', 9fin, 18-Jun-2026, https://9fin.com/news/1588af65-5d5c-476d-aed1-ac5ad043a0a8
transaction_summary.use_of_proceeds: Refinance the Group's approximately GBP 630m (equivalent) Senior Notes due 2027 (EUR 370m 4.5% and $410m 6.625% tranches sitting at Motion Bondco DAC), for general corporate purposes, and to pay associated transaction costs and expenses. Tender/redemption mechanics for the SUNs (e.g. make-whole, tender price, consent solicitation structure) are not available - further diligence required; likely source: tender offer memorandum / redemption notice once launched. No indication in reviewed sources that any SUN holders are being left out of the takeout - market commentary describes the deal as pricing 'a full take-out at par'. Source: Merlin RNS, 10-Sep-2026; 'Merlin refis SUNs as temporary fix...', 9fin, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/7bbf2ed4-3a88-48dd-aaf8-3752b643a9d3
transaction_summary.lender_group: Led by Monarch Alternative Capital and GoldenTree Asset Management according to 9fin sources. Oaktree Capital was separately reported as one of the private credit funds involved in the original proposal (late August 2026). Arini (a London-based hedge fund) was approached for comment in 9fin's coverage of the deal, reflecting its active CDS/bond positioning around Merlin, though its role (if any) as a facility lender is not confirmed. The New Term Facility is fully committed by institutional investors, with a portion reserved for existing creditors to participate in via syndication - the identities and allocation of that syndicate are not available - further diligence required; likely source: syndication documentation / allocation notice. Source: 'Goldentree and Monarch lead Merlin refi...', 9fin, 17-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/d2468584-df61-4bbb-99c2-19d9a2fc68de; 'Merlin sets up private credit refi proposal', 9fin, 28-Aug-2026, https://9fin.com/news/1f46813f-5336-43e6-9187-0de5eedc4dc1; 'Merlin confirms GBP 657m secured refi of 2027 SUNs', 9fin, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/b9ef800a-31a3-4e7d-9597-8492eac34786
transaction_summary.conditions_and_timing: Commitment documentation signed; completion subject to customary closing conditions and currently expected to close by the end of 2026. Source: Merlin RNS, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/documents/ae93bb0a-d42e-4872-a856-3aefdaf949a1

advisers.company_side: PJT Partners (financial adviser) and Kirkland & Ellis (legal counsel, initially engaged via its capital markets rather than restructuring team). Source: 'Merlin confirms GBP 657m secured refi of 2027 SUNs', 9fin, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/b9ef800a-31a3-4e7d-9597-8492eac34786; 'How might Merlin tackle upcoming SUN maturities?', 9fin, 19-Jun-2026, https://9fin.com/news/22e48f42-cd8c-4d57-8958-51a0e50501d9
advisers.secured_lender_side: A group of Merlin's secured lenders (holding a slice of the GBP 3.2bn secured debt stack) is advised by Gibson Dunn. Teneo separately pitched for a creditor-side advisory role outside a potential Gibson Dunn-led co-op. Source: 'Merlin confirms GBP 657m secured refi of 2027 SUNs', 9fin, 10-Sep-2026; 'How might Merlin tackle upcoming SUN maturities?', 9fin, 19-Jun-2026
advisers.new_facility_lender_side: not available - further diligence required (advisers to Monarch/GoldenTree/Oaktree group not disclosed in reviewed sources)

market_reception.bonds: SUNs rallied roughly 3 points in the days around announcement (euro tranche indicated at 99.84, US tranche at 98.08 by 10-Sep), effectively pricing a full take-out at par. By contrast the 2030, 2031 and 2032 SSNs sold off, falling around 5 points to the mid-to-high 70s in the days around the news, before partially recovering (2030s regained ~2 points to near 75, 2032s similarly, by 16-Sep) as some investors concluded the removal of the near-term maturity wall outweighed the dilution from the new collateral package. Source: 'Goldentree and Monarch lead Merlin refi...', 9fin, 17-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/d2468584-df61-4bbb-99c2-19d9a2fc68de; 'Merlin confirms GBP 657m secured refi of 2027 SUNs', 9fin, 10-Sep-2026
market_reception.cds: Motion Bondco DAC CDS is set to (re)join the iTraxx Crossover index (series 46) on 21-Sep-2026, having been removed with the series 44-to-45 roll in March 2026 after the August 2025 S&P downgrade. CDS spreads, previously above 500bps, had tightened sharply on 'orphaning' fears (that Merlin could repay the referenced bonds while issuing debt elsewhere in the structure, leaving CDS protection economically stranded) but were bid back up around the refinancing news as some investors concluded default risk had fallen and orphaning risk was less likely to be exercised. Source: 'Goldentree and Monarch lead Merlin refi...', 9fin, 17-Sep-2026; 'Arini trades Merlin Entertainment SUNs CDS', 9fin, 18-Jun-2026, https://9fin.com/news/1588af65-5d5c-476d-aed1-ac5ad043a0a8
market_reception.buyside_commentary: Investors quoted by 9fin were split: one noted the collateral pool was narrower than feared ('they did not have to give that much extra security to be fair'); a second called it a maturity extension that 'does not resolve the underlying operating trajectory' and said 'we will be back at the table in a year or so unless operations really improve'; a third called it a 'band-aid solution' pending a fuller capital structure fix. Source: 'Merlin confirms GBP 657m secured refi of 2027 SUNs', 9fin, 10-Sep-2026, https://9fin.com/news/b9ef800a-31a3-4e7d-9597-8492eac34786

rating_agency_response.moodys: 16-Sep-2026: Moody's changed Merlin's outlook to negative and downgraded its senior secured instrument ratings to Caa2, while affirming the Caa1 corporate family rating. This places the senior secured rating below the CFR, consistent with the new facility's additional collateral diluting recoveries available to the pre-existing secured stack. Full rationale text not available - further diligence required (Moody's press release paywalled/inaccessible); likely source: Moody's subscriber portal. Source: 9fin latest news feed, event dated 2026-09-16, https://www.moodys.com/research/docid--PR_529507
rating_agency_response.sp: 14-Sep-2026: S&P placed Motion Midco's 'B-' senior secured debt rating on CreditWatch Negative. Full rationale not available - further diligence required; likely source: S&P subscriber portal. This follows S&P's downgrade of Motion Midco (the CFR-level entity) to CCC+ in August 2025, driven by H1 2025 operational underperformance (reported EBITDA down 10.8% YoY). Source: 9fin latest news feed, event dated 2026-09-14, https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/3626934; 'Motion sickness as Merlin Entertainments suffers triple-C downgrade', 9fin, 20-Aug-2025, https://9fin.com/news/939bbe37-4dfb-4e5d-aa3f-cd1b14b665db
rating_agency_response.fitch: not available - further diligence required. No Fitch rating action on Merlin identified in 9fin's news feed or document search for this period; likely source: Fitch subscriber portal, if Merlin is Fitch-rated at all (not confirmed)

transaction_summary.existing_ssn_tlb_holder_reaction: No formal creditor co-op or litigation threat identified specifically in response to the new facility. A group of secured lenders/bondholders (advised by Gibson Dunn, with Teneo also having pitched for a role) had been organising since at least mid-2026 in anticipation of a transaction, but 9fin sources note this group had not sent a term sheet as a group and the outreach was described as 'accurate but limited in scope', expected to address only the 2027 SUNs. Post-announcement commentary from secured-side investors was concerned but not adversarial (see buyside_commentary above) - focused on recovery dilution rather than legal challenge. Source: 'Merlin mandates PJT to advise on forthcoming maturities', 9fin, 27-Aug-2026, https://9fin.com/news/111a555a-67d0-4844-90fb-e8897fbc75e2; 'Merlin Entertainments fields pitches from firms eyeing 2027 debt maturity', 9fin, 25-Aug-2026, https://9fin.com/news/ca298053-0425-4881-be1c-928ae0b617f6
alternatives_considered: Asset disposals: completed sale of Lego Discovery Centres/Legoland Discovery Centres to the Lego Group, completed February 2026, generating GBP 216m net cash proceeds (GBP 221m gross, GBP 68m after-tax profit), used to pay down the RCF. An earlier planned sale of UK aquarium assets was reportedly shelved in 2025/early 2026 due to limited buyer interest. Source: 'Merlin lenders review debt documentation', 9fin, 21-Jan-2026, https://9fin.com/news/21fe3089-e114-4a70-858a-9a47dc4f4c46; 'Merlin Entertainments actively evaluates refi options', 9fin, 21-May-2026, https://9fin.com/news/336ddb30-6012-45ea-8a63-e1e9ab3f6c61

Sale-and-leaseback of freehold assets and/or new debt raised against unencumbered freeholds (estimated by 9fin at roughly GBP 0.7bn sitting at non-guarantor level based on the 2032 SSN OM disclosure) - explored by the market as an option but not the route ultimately taken (the new facility used previously unencumbered leasehold/operating assets - London Eye, SEA LIFE London, Shrek's Adventure!, UK Dungeons - as collateral rather than a sale-leaseback). Source: 'How might Merlin tackle upcoming SUN maturities?', 9fin, 19-Jun-2026, https://9fin.com/news/22e48f42-cd8c-4d57-8958-51a0e50501d9

A new public high-yield bond offering, a TLB extension, and a partial shareholder equity injection by Blackstone/KIRKBI/CPPIB were all cited by 9fin sources as options under consideration alongside asset sales - none of these were the route ultimately taken; the sponsors' public statement alongside the announcement confirmed they are 'fully supportive' of management's strategy but did not reference an equity injection into this transaction. Source: 'Arini trades Merlin Entertainment SUNs CDS', 9fin, 18-Jun-2026, https://9fin.com/news/1588af65-5d5c-476d-aed1-ac5ad043a0a8; Merlin RNS, 10-Sep-2026

analysis_pieces.title: Merlin refis SUNs as temporary fix - Mid-term cap stack risk remains (9fin, 10-Sep-2026)
analysis_pieces.key_findings: The GBP 657m refinancing removes the near-term 2027 maturity wall but does not fix the underlying credit story. H1 2026 underlying revenue was down 2.2% reported (flat at constant currency); EBITDA fell to GBP 170m reported but rose 0.8% constant-currency, margin flat at 21%. Performance is sharply regional: North America inflected strongly (revenue +5.9% cc, EBITDA +20.6%, margin up to 32.2%) on the back of Lego Galaxy openings; the UK deteriorated further (revenue -5.8%, EBITDA -26.2%, margin down to 20.4%) on weak consumer confidence, high Q2 temperatures and softer London Gateway tourism; International (Europe + Asia Pacific) grew modestly (+1.5% cc revenue, +1.0% EBITDA). The LDC disposal (GBP 216m net proceeds, Feb 2026) materially improved the cash cycle and funded a GBP 120m RCF paydown, cutting RCF drawings to GBP 40m at 27-Jun-2026 from GBP 160m at FY25. Reported net debt (incl. leases) GBP 5.42bn, net leverage 9.5x (vs 9.7x Q1 26, 9.6x FY25); 9fin estimates leverage ex-LDC contribution at ~10.1x on a ~GBP 535m EBITDA base. The residual secured stack will carry a higher blended coupon against a business that remains structurally FCF negative; the 2029-2032 maturities face refinancing focus in 2028 at double-digit leverage, which 9fin flags could require a more holistic capital structure restructuring.

analysis_pieces.title: Goldentree and Monarch lead Merlin refi as bonds and CDS take different rides (9fin, 17-Sep-2026)
analysis_pieces.key_findings: Confirms Monarch Alternative Capital and GoldenTree Asset Management as lead arrangers of the new $396m/EUR 418m facility, priced at 650bps over benchmark, six-year maturity with a springing maturity to before 2030 if other debt is not refinanced. Highlights the divergent post-announcement price action between SUNs (rallied) and 2030/2031/2032 SSNs (sold off, then partially recovered), attributing this to the market pricing in recovery dilution for existing secured holders from the new UK asset collateral package. Notes estimated net leverage now around 10x and that Merlin may need to consider a more holistic cap-structure restructuring heading into the next refinancing round. Also covers the reinstatement of Motion Bondco DAC CDS into iTraxx Crossover series 46 (21-Sep-2026) and improving CDS sentiment as default risk is perceived to have fallen.

analysis_pieces.title: How might Merlin tackle upcoming SUN maturities? (9fin, 19-Jun-2026)
analysis_pieces.key_findings: Pre-transaction options analysis. Estimated ~GBP 0.7bn of unencumbered assets sitting at non-guarantor level (based on the 2032 SSN OM), potentially available for new structurally senior debt. SSN collateral is structural (share pledges/intercompany receivables) rather than direct asset mortgages, meaning freehold assets are technically saleable. Flagged options: new public HY offering, TLB extension, partial shareholder equity injection, sale-and-leaseback, or a combination. Noted Kirkland & Ellis's mandate was via its capital markets team (not restructuring), suggesting at the time a regular-way refinancing rather than an LME was the base case. Q1 26 EBITDA GBP 555m LTM, net debt ~GBP 5.375bn, leverage 9.7x, with 'meaningful covenant headroom and access to its revolver' cited by bulls.

analysis_pieces.title: CLOs sit on Merlin SUN positions ahead of private credit refi (9fin, 08-Sep-2026)
analysis_pieces.key_findings: CLO managers (TPG/Northwoods, Blackstone, Fidelity, Investcorp, King Street) held material SUN positions ahead of the refinancing, an unusual concentration given CLOs' typical loan focus and unsecured exposure limits; CVC sold down its Cordatus CLO SUN position at 96 in June. Confirms Q1 26 LTM EBITDA of GBP 555m against GBP 5.38bn net debt for 9.7x net leverage (vs 9.6x Q4 25), with senior secured net leverage of 5.6x - comfortably inside a 10x springing covenant, though moving in the wrong direction. Notes the SUNs traded near par pricing a full take-out, while the SSNs at mid-to-high 70s reflected a materially weaker read on the credit once the unsecured tranche moves higher in priority via the new facility.

situation_overview: Merlin Entertainments is a UK-headquartered, Blackstone/KIRKBI/CPPIB-backed operator of 131 family entertainment attractions across 22 countries, including 11 Legoland resorts, five resort theme parks, the London Eye and 45 SEA LIFE sites. FY 2025 revenue was around GBP 2bn on 60 million guests. The credit has been under sustained pressure since 2024-2025: a slow post-pandemic recovery, heavy capex requirements, and free cash flow burn drove a series of downgrades through 2025, culminating in an S&P cut to CCC+ (August 2025) after H1 2025 reported EBITDA fell 10.8% YoY and visits declined roughly 4%. Performance through H1 2026 has diverged sharply by region: North America has inflected positively, with Q2/H1 2026 revenue up 5.9% at constant currency and EBITDA up 20.6%, driven by the February/March 2026 Lego Galaxy openings at Legoland California and Legoland Florida (GBP 70m combined capex) and workforce/procurement savings. The UK, by contrast, has deteriorated further, with H1 2026 revenue down 5.8% and EBITDA down 26.2%, hit by weak consumer confidence, unusually high Q2 temperatures, softer inbound tourism to London Gateway attractions, and revenue-timing effects from the shift to annual passes; management also cited the earlier 2026 Iran war/Middle East conflict as dampening international travel confidence and visitor numbers in Q1 2026. International (Europe plus Asia Pacific, combined from 2026) grew modestly. Group underlying EBITDA margin has held broadly stable around 21%. The company completed the sale of its Lego and Legoland Discovery Centres to the Lego Group in February 2026 for GBP 216m net cash proceeds, which it used to pay down GBP 120m of RCF drawings (RCF drawn fell to GBP 40m at 27-Jun-2026 from GBP 160m at FY 2025), a helpful but one-off deleveraging and liquidity action rather than organic improvement. Reported net leverage stood at 9.5x at H1 2026 (9.7x Q1 2026, 9.6x FY 2025); 9fin estimates leverage on a cleaner, ex-LDC EBITDA base at closer to 10.1x. Against this backdrop, Merlin spent H1 2026 negotiating a refinancing of its GBP 630m (equivalent) senior unsecured notes due November 2027, which was announced on 10 September 2026 as a GBP 657m senior secured term loan (see transaction_summary). The deal removes the immediate 2027 maturity wall but, per 9fin's own analysis and buyside commentary, is widely viewed in the market as a 'band-aid' that extends the maturity profile without resolving the underlying operating and leverage trajectory - the residual 2029-2032 secured maturities will come into refinancing focus in 2028 against a still double-digit leverage base and a business that remains structurally free cash flow negative once the higher coupon on the new facility (est. ~GBP 30m of incremental annual interest) is layered in. Q3 2026, Merlin's peak trading quarter, is the next key credit test: sustained North American momentum and UK stabilisation would support delivery of full-year revenue growth guidance, while further UK deterioration would be a significant mid-term credit challenge notwithstanding the removal of the near-term maturity wall.

key_catalysts.liquidity: Available liquidity was approximately GBP 476m at end-Q1 2026 (GBP 113m cash plus GBP 363m undrawn on the GBP 428m RCF, net of GBP 20m utilised in letters of credit). By H1 2026 (27-Jun-2026), RCF drawings had fallen further to GBP 40m (from GBP 160m at FY 2025) following the GBP 120m paydown funded by LDC disposal proceeds, implying stronger headroom into the seasonal peak, though a precise H1 2026 cash balance and total liquidity figure were not found in the sources reviewed - not available - further diligence required, likely source: H1 2026 Results Statement / Q2 2026 Financial Report (9fin document IDs de376b7c-bbb4-4740-bed3-1d4402fd28fb and b19069c3-e6af-42da-b980-4961ff7f613c). The business remains structurally free cash flow negative per 9fin's analysis, which is the key medium-term liquidity risk even though near-term facility headroom looks adequate.

management.name: Fiona Eastwood
management.experience: Joined Merlin in 2015 as Global Marketing Director for Gateway Attractions; served as COO of the global attractions business 2019-2024 (Gateway attractions globally, Resort Theme Parks UK/Europe); appointed interim CEO November 2024 following Scott O'Neil's departure, confirmed as permanent CEO February 2025. Prior experience at BBC Worldwide. Over 25 years in consumer-facing brand/marketing/strategy roles. recommendation.rationale: Merlin should remain on the restructuring watchlist despite the successful completion of the 2027 SUN refinancing. The September 2026 transaction removes the immediate maturity trigger but does not address the underlying drivers of distress: reported net leverage of 9.5x at H1 2026 (an estimated ~10.1x on a cleaner ex-LDC EBITDA base), a business that 9fin's own analysis describes as structurally free cash flow negative, and a residual GBP 3.2bn+ secured stack (TLBs due 2029, SSNs due 2030-2032) that will need refinancing in 2028 at what is currently double-digit leverage - a maturity wall the market does not yet see as clearly refinanceable on current trajectory, as reflected in the sell-off in the 2030/2031/2032 SSNs and the Moody's/S&P rating actions taken in the same week as the deal closed. Buyside sources quoted by 9fin explicitly frame the transaction as a 'band-aid' rather than a fix, expecting to be 'back at the table in a year or so' absent an operational turnaround. Covenant headroom is currently adequate (senior secured net leverage of 5.6x sits well inside the 10x springing covenant, and RCF drawings of ~9% are far below the 40% springing covenant trigger), so a near-term covenant trip is not the active risk. Liquidity also looks adequate for now (GBP 476m at Q1 2026, materially higher headroom on the RCF at H1 2026 following the LDC disposal-funded paydown), so an immediate liquidity crisis is not imminent either. The primary trigger is therefore the leverage/maturity wall: high and rising secured leverage against a persistently negative free cash flow profile, with the 2028 refinancing of the 2029-2032 stack the key date to monitor, alongside continued UK segment deterioration as the swing factor for FY 2026 guidance delivery.
triggers: Leverage / maturity wall that cannot be easily refinanced (primary trigger - residual 2029-2032 secured stack refinancing due 2028 against ~10x leverage and negative FCF)
Liquidity issue (secondary, forward-looking - structurally negative free cash flow could erode current adequate headroom over time)
